text:
Kite — window chrome styles.
   Colors come from CSS variables set per Space (see theme.ts).

---- design tokens ---------------------------------------------------------
   Shape, depth and motion shared by every part of the window.
   Motion follows the HyperFrames motion rules, adapted to an interface:
   arrivals land on a long-tailed ease-out, exits are ~45% shorter and ease in,
   moves that start and stop on screen ease both ways. Only opacity, transform
   and filter animate; nothing idles, floats or pulses.
A Space's pattern (Glow, Dots, Grid, Lines, Rings): soft marks over its colours.
Must receive the pointer even where the strip around the page drags the window.
---- favorites ----

No Favorites yet: no empty box. While you drag a tab, a drop slot appears over the
   Space name for the moment of the drag, so nothing in the list moves.
Arc's favourites: soft translucent tiles; the open one turns solid with a gentle lift.
---- space header ----
Arc: the Space's name is a quiet label over its tabs, not a headline.

Drop indicators, as in Arc / macOS outline views: a line with a small ring at its start,
   indented to the level the item will land at.
"On" a folder: the folder lights up, and so does everything already in it.
Picked rows (⌘-click / ⇧-click), like Arc's multi-select.
The folder's "…" waits until you point at the folder; its count steps aside.
A closed folder still shows its open tab, just under it (Arc's "peek").
"Drop here to pin" shows only mid-drag, laid over the divider below, so the list never shifts.
Arc's "↓ Clear" waits until you point at the divider; the line steps aside for it.

The strip around the page moves the window. (There used to be a 36px empty band
   here for the window buttons; they now live in the sidebar and hide with it.)
With no space around the page, a hairline at the top still lets you move the window.
A theme change floods the card's colour, easing both ways.
---- empty state ----
The kite drifts in and settles once; after that it is still.
Reduce Motion (Kite's switch): see the matching system-preference block below.
---- find bar ----
Arrivals that rise a few pixels as they fade in: the load-error card, download and extension rows.
While dragging, pages must not swallow the pointer.
---- spaces ----
The Welcome tour.
---- archive ----
---- command bar results ----
---- split view ----
---- little window ----
---- boosts ----
---- routing ----
---- import ----

---- settings ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Two panes: a quiet nav column (search + sections) and a scrolling page of cards.
   Each card is a list of rows: what it is on the left, its control on the right.
Settings is a page that fills the page area (the sidebar stays beside it).
While Settings is open, the sidebar's selected tab isn't what you're looking at.
Arc's Settings: the window's name, a row of icon tabs in the middle, search on the right.
One centred column; sections 44px apart, groups 20px apart, all on an 8px rhythm.
Arc's nudge at the top of General.
Narrower windows: the title goes first, then the search gets smaller, then the tab labels tighten.
A titled card of rows.
a control that no longer fits beside its label drops below it, never over it
the label keeps at least this much room before the control wraps under it
A row that opens another panel.
Sheets never grow past the window; their body scrolls instead.
A narrow page area (small window, wide sidebar): the section list becomes icons.
---- playing / muted indicator ----
---- Floating video controls, design D (its own see-through window) ----

Almost invisible, but clearly not transparent to macOS: so this window takes the
   mouse (a nearly-zero alpha can count as "see-through" and let clicks fall through
   to Chromium's window underneath, which then shows its own buttons and grey shade).

Always-on thin dark edge, exactly on the video's outline (curved when it is): it hides
   the light rim macOS draws around the window, so no pale line shows at the corners.

Arc's floating-video palette: a dark chip (#212123) edged by a 20% white hairline.
   This window sits over Chromium's video window, so a backdrop blur has nothing to
   sample; the chips are near-opaque instead of frosted.
Controls settle in from slightly off their spot as they appear.
---- Top bar ----
---- Play and skips ----
---- Scrubber bar ----
---- Small videos: just the essentials (Arc's compact size class) ----
Resize from any edge or corner.

The seek slider: a native range input (drag, click, keyboard) over a drawn track.
   It thickens under the mouse and while you drag (Arc's grow-on-hover).
---- Mini player: a compact card; drag it anywhere ----
Sleeping tabs: their page is unloaded to save memory.

==== Motion ====================================================================
   Built on the tokens at the top (--ease-out, --ease-in, --ease-move) and the
   user's feel (--ease) and speed (--dur, --speed). Reduce Motion turns all of it off.

Switching tabs is instant: it happens hundreds of times a day, and any motion
   there reads as latency. The sidebar row, not the page, shows the change.
Sheets arrive slightly low and small, and settle.
A docked sheet (Customize): at the side, nothing dimmed, the window stays usable behind it.
It keeps clear of the sidebar: on the other side when the sidebar is on the right.
The command bar (⌘T) appears at once, like Raycast: it is the most-used thing in Kite.

Rows move with FLIP (renderer/flip.ts): a row that is pinned, unpinned, dropped or
   left behind by a closed neighbour glides to its place; a new row slides in. Nothing
   re-animates when a Space's whole list mounts: the pane's own slide carries that.
The hidden sidebar slides out on a long tail and leaves faster, easing in.
Pressing things gives a little; hover responds at once.
Tabs and favourites settle back on a spring once released (theme.ts → --press-ease).
Going in is quick; only the release springs.
A short stagger (the cards read as one list), capped so the page settles within ~250 ms.
==== Address bar: security and Shields ====================================
The domain in full ink, the rest of the address faded (Arc shows only the domain).

Site controls sit at the right end and appear when you point at the address bar;
   whatever else is on the right makes room for them.
Asking before a cancel: the row itself turns into the question.
The number beside each Downloads filter.
Keyboard users always see where they are.
Text fields share one focus look with the start page and Settings search: a soft accent ring.
Sidebar top: the sidebar switch sits by the window buttons, navigation at the far end.
Small windows: the sidebar gives way to the page instead of taking over a third of it.
People who ask their system for more contrast get firmer lines and text.
Icons: a lighter stroke sits better next to 13px text.
Slim, quiet scrollbars in panels.
Range sliders: an accent fill and a clear thumb.
Kite follows the system's Reduce Motion setting as well as its own.

The system's Reduce Motion: fewer and gentler, not none. Nothing slides, scales or
   blurs; sheets and menus fade in briefly; hover, press and toggle colours still answer.
Settings search: the matching setting is marked for a moment.
The command bar and find bar are focus themselves: no extra box around their text field.
The Settings button stays lit while the Settings page is open, so you know where you are.
Says who a page changes: the whole window, or just this Space.

==== Start page (new tab, and the window with nothing open) ====================
   Hierarchy: greeting (quiet) → search box (the hero) → Favorites → Frequently visited.
   Motion follows the HyperFrames rules: the greeting blurs in, the box rises on a long
   tail, tiles cascade 40 ms apart; nothing loops, only opacity, transform and blur move.
The Kite mark lives in the box: the brand where your attention already is.
above the box's soft focus ring, so the seam is one clean line
the focused box lifts 1px; follow it
hide its top edge so box and list share one line
Cascade in: each tile 40 ms after the one before (capped).
A toast leaves faster than it arrived, easing in (HyperFrames: exits are ~45% shorter).
The mark tilts into place as the bar opens, then holds still.
Empty states share one pattern: an icon in a soft circle, a title, then a line of help.
Sheets leave too: faster than they came, easing in (HyperFrames: exits ~45% shorter).
One brand mark everywhere: an app-icon chip in the Space's accent with a white kite.
Site names may take two lines so "Hacker News" isn't cut off.
On a dark picture: light text, with a soft shadow so it reads on busy spots.
---- colour wheel (the Space theme editor) ----
---- Settings → Ad blocking (AdBlock.tsx) ----
---- site popover: what was blocked ----
The per-site list of protections: what is on and what is off for this page.
==== Kite's own UI failed: a plain, readable recovery screen ==================
A screen still loading its code (a few ms from disk): hold its place quietly.
==== Guidelines pass: scroll containment, balanced headings, menu origin ========
A menu grows out of the corner nearest the pointer (set inline when it flips to fit).
==== Home page: scenes, engine chip, shortcuts, widgets, customize ==============
The Space's picture behind the whole home page; text and controls follow its tone.
On a dark picture, chrome reads light.
The engine you search with, switchable in place.
The add-shortcut tile and the in-place editor.
Widgets.
On a scene the card is dark glass, so every child (buttons, inputs, lines, greys) takes light inks.
Clock
Weather
Note
To-do
Calendar
Timer
The customize button.
Quiet until you reach for it: a small ghost button that takes the accent on hover.
Small shared pieces: a section heading used by Downloads, site info and Extensions, and an inline slider row.
The Space theme editor: three rows of swatches, the wheel, intensity, grain and mode.
The same editor inside Settings › Spaces.
Collapse / Expand Pinned Section: a chevron on the divider, shown on hover; always shown while collapsed, with the count.
A built-in picture behind the window: the frame shows it, the sidebar frosts it.
Picture choices in the theme editor: small landscape tiles, the name on hover or when chosen.
The Pinned chevron sits over the start of the divider until it is needed, so the line keeps its inset.
Over a picture the shortcut hints sit on a small frosted pill, readable on any part of the scene.
Hidden from sight, still reachable by keyboard and screen readers.
Upload tile: a dashed slot in the picture grid.
Your own gradient: a preview bar, its colours, and the angle.
Accelerated downloads: IDM's segmented bar (each connection fills its own range) and a small bolt on the icon.
